set.body:
Why
NumPy iterator machinery earns its keep on awkward views through dimension coalescing, contiguous inner runs, and cache-aware traversal. Ravel already has compact LoopPlan paths, but remaining inner-strided, transposed, reversed, and mixed-broadcast losses may justify a more capable general planner.

Scope
- Use the court to localize planner losses by physical density, inner-run length, stride pattern, dtype width, and operation cost.
- Extend LoopPlan only with general transformations such as dimension coalescing, direct contiguous inner runs, bounded tiling, or cache-aware outer traversal.
- Preserve logical result order, C-order allocating output, deterministic reduction order, overlap rules, and exact view semantics. Reordering is allowed only when the operation contract makes it observationally irrelevant.
- Select thresholds from workload classes and hardware facts, never benchmark identities or exact fixture shapes. Keep small-array paths compact.

Scala.js impact
Shared strided planning can help typed-array locality, but JavaScript branch and object costs differ from the JVM. Node must prove each new plan shape separately; a JVM win may retain the old Scala.js path. Browser correctness and fullLink are mandatory. Do not assume CPU cache tuning transfers unchanged through V8.

Acceptance
- Receipts cover offset-contiguous, inner-strided, outer-strided, transposed, reversed, broadcast, mixed-sign, and small irregular views across multiple shapes and dtypes.
- A promoted plan improves its targeted public class at least 1.20x, keeps planning allocation bounded, and causes no unexplained regression above 10 percent.
- Semantic and layout signatures remain exact on JVM and Scala.js.
- Reductions preserve the existing canonical pairwise result bit-for-bit where that contract applies.
- Standard cross-platform and fullLink gates pass.
set.title: Make strided traversal cache-aware without semantic reordering
